philosophy: runner pullbacks (the flip side of squad 8) and industry waves among large caps (breadth thrusts, leader then followers)
preRegistered: squad13-core.mjs RULES + TH (24 Oct 2026, before any run) + data/strategy-library.json SQ13-*
standard: both halves (signal before / from 2024-01-01): > 0 after 0.8% and 1.2% cost, better than the average liquid stock over the same sessions, better than the same stock on its other days, > 0 without the 2 best, 20+ trades and 3+ blocks (blocks = the hold), block t >= 2.5, return per year of capital above SPY on the same days -> TRADABLE SMALL; block t >= 4.07 -> PROVEN. Gross returns capped at +300% for trades and yardsticks alike (AUD-1).

SQ13-RPB.name: Runner pullback: a 10-day runner bought on its first 8-15% pullback within 5-15 sessions, above its base and 20-day average (hold 20)
SQ13-RPB.rule: RUNNER at the close of t (squad 8 base, unchanged: liquid; 10-session gain +15% to +100%; the first session it crosses +15%; complete data). PULLBACK: H_u = the highest close from t to u; the signal is the FIRST session u in t+5..t+15 with 0.85 x H_u <= close_u <= 0.92 x H_u (8-15% off the post-run high), close_u above the pre-run base (close of t-10) and above its 20-session average, liquid at u. The setup is void if before u any close (t+1..u-1) fell under 0.85 x H or under the pre-run base. Buy the open of u+1; hold 20 sessions; one open trade per stock.

papers.cite: Jegadeesh (1990) Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns, Journal of Finance 45(3) (one-month reversal)
Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers, Journal of Finance 48(1)
O'Neil, How to Make Money in Stocks (4th ed., 2009): buy a leader on its first orderly pullback, not extended (practitioner)

SQ13-RPB-CLEAN.name: Runner pullback with clean supply: share count up at most 1% a year, no reverse split in 3 years (hold 20)
SQ13-RPB-CLEAN.rule: SQ13-RPB signal AND the SEC share count known at u (30 days late, split-repaired, dated within 200 days of its cut-off) is at most 1% above the count known 365 days earlier AND no reverse split (Massive split list, to < from) executed in the 1,095 days up to u. Buy the open of u+1; hold 20; one open trade per stock.

papers.cite: Jegadeesh (1990) Evidence of Predictable Behavior of Security Returns, Journal of Finance 45(3) (one-month reversal)
Pontiff & Woodgate (2008) Share Issuance and Cross-sectional Returns, Journal of Finance 63(2)
Martell & Webb (2008) The performance of stocks that are reverse split, Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting 30

SQ13-RPB-BUYBACK.name: Runner pullback with buybacks: share count down 2%+ in a year, no reverse split in 3 years (hold 20)
SQ13-RPB-BUYBACK.rule: SQ13-RPB signal AND the SEC share count known at u is at least 2% below (and not below 60% of) the count known 365 days earlier AND no reverse split in the 1,095 days up to u. Buy the open of u+1; hold 20; one open trade per stock.

papers.cite: Ikenberry, Lakonishok & Vermaelen (1995) Market underreaction to open market share repurchases, Journal of Financial Economics 39(2-3)
Pontiff & Woodgate (2008) Share Issuance and Cross-sectional Returns, Journal of Finance 63(2)
Martell & Webb (2008) The performance of stocks that are reverse split, Review of Quantitative Finance and Accounting 30

SQ13-RPB-LARGE.name: Large-cap runner pullback: the same pullback among the 500 largest, held a quarter (hold 63)
SQ13-RPB-LARGE.rule: RUNNER at the close of t (squad 8 base, unchanged: liquid; 10-session gain +15% to +100%; the first session it crosses +15%; complete data) AND the stock is among the 500 liquid stocks with the highest 63-session average traded value at t. PULLBACK: H_u = the highest close from t to u; the signal is the FIRST session u in t+5..t+15 with 0.85 x H_u <= close_u <= 0.92 x H_u (8-15% off the post-run high), close_u above the pre-run base (close of t-10) and above its 20-session average, liquid at u. The setup is void if before u any close (t+1..u-1) fell under 0.85 x H or under the pre-run base. Buy the open of u+1; hold 63 sessions; one open trade per stock.

papers.cite: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers, Journal of Finance 48(1)
O'Neil, How to Make Money in Stocks (4th ed., 2009): buy a leader on its first orderly pullback, not extended (practitioner)
Hou (2007) Industry Information Diffusion and the Lead-lag Effect in Stock Returns, Review of Financial Studies 20(4) (big firms lead small firms of the same industry)

SQ13-WAVE-BIG.name: Industry wave among large caps (breadth under 40% -> over 60% within a month): buy its 3 largest, hold 63
SQ13-WAVE-BIG.rule: Daily at the close of t. Universe U_t = the 1,000 liquid stocks with the highest 63-session average traded value; industry = SIC 3-digit; breadth = share of the industry's U_t members (8+ needed, each with a 50-session average) closing above their 50-session average. WAVE at t: breadth > 60% at t AND under 40% on at least one session of t-21..t-1 (8+ members then too) AND no wave of that industry in the 63 sessions before t. Buy the open of t+1 the industry's 3 members of U_t with the highest 63-session average traded value; hold 63 sessions; one open trade per stock.

papers.cite: Zweig (1986) Winning on Wall Street: the breadth thrust (advancing share from under 40% to over 61.5% within 10 days) (practitioner)
Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) Do Industries Explain Momentum? Journal of Finance 54(4)
Hou (2007) Industry Information Diffusion and the Lead-lag Effect in Stock Returns, Review of Financial Studies 20(4) (big firms lead small firms of the same industry)

SQ13-WAVE-STRONG.name: Industry wave among large caps: buy its 3 strongest members (63-session return), hold 63
SQ13-WAVE-STRONG.rule: Daily at the close of t. Universe U_t = the 1,000 liquid stocks with the highest 63-session average traded value; industry = SIC 3-digit; breadth = share of the industry's U_t members (8+ needed, each with a 50-session average) closing above their 50-session average. WAVE at t: breadth > 60% at t AND under 40% on at least one session of t-21..t-1 (8+ members then too) AND no wave of that industry in the 63 sessions before t. Buy the open of t+1 the industry's 3 members of U_t with the highest 63-session return (close t / close t-63); hold 63 sessions; one open trade per stock.

papers.cite: Zweig (1986) Winning on Wall Street: the breadth thrust (advancing share from under 40% to over 61.5% within 10 days) (practitioner)
Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) Do Industries Explain Momentum? Journal of Finance 54(4)
Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers, Journal of Finance 48(1)

SQ13-LEADF.name: Leader then followers: the industry's largest member makes a new 52-week high right after its results 8-K; buy the next 2-4 largest that have not moved (hold 63)
SQ13-LEADF.rule: Industry (SIC 3-digit) with 4+ members in U_t (the 1,000 largest by 63-session traded value). LEADER = its member with the highest 63-session traded value at t. The leader files an 8-K with item 2.02 (results; SEC submissions, filing date F); r0 = the first session on or after F. Signal at the close of the FIRST t in r0+1..r0+3 (always after the filing, whatever its hour) where the leader is still the leader and closes above its PRE-RESULTS 52-week high (the highest close of the 252 sessions before r0, 240+ present). FOLLOWERS = the industry's members ranked 2, 3 and 4 by traded value at t whose return from the close of r0-1 to the close of t is under +2%. Buy them at the open of t+1; hold 63 sessions; one open trade per stock.

papers.cite: Hou (2007) Industry Information Diffusion and the Lead-lag Effect in Stock Returns, Review of Financial Studies 20(4) (big firms lead small firms of the same industry)
Thomas & Zhang (2008) Overreaction to Intra-industry Information Transfers? Journal of Accounting Research 46(4) (early reporters' news moves later peers)
Foster (1981) Intra-industry information transfers associated with earnings releases, Journal of Accounting and Economics 3(3)

SQ13-LEADH.name: Leader breakout then followers: the industry's largest member makes its first 52-week high in 63 sessions; buy the next 2-4 largest that have not moved (hold 63)
SQ13-LEADH.rule: Industry (SIC 3-digit) with 4+ members in U_t; LEADER = the member with the highest 63-session traded value at t. Signal at the close of t when the leader closes above the highest close of its previous 252 sessions (240+ present) and did NOT do so on any of the 63 sessions before t. FOLLOWERS = members ranked 2, 3 and 4 at t whose 10-session return (close t / close t-10) is under +2%. Buy them at the open of t+1; hold 63 sessions; one open trade per stock. (No results filing needed: the price-only twin of SQ13-LEADF.)

papers.cite: Hou (2007) Industry Information Diffusion and the Lead-lag Effect in Stock Returns, Review of Financial Studies 20(4) (big firms lead small firms of the same industry)
George & Hwang (2004) The 52-Week High and Momentum Investing, Journal of Finance 59(5)
